topic: Graph-recursive formula-or-ambiguity certificates for fine-grid causal transfers from subsampled Gaussian process DAGs. Let X_t=A X_{t-1}+ε_t be a stable stationary Gaussian VAR(1) with positive diagonal innovation covariance and a supplied labeled lower-triangular cross-variable DAG; observe only Y_s=X_{ms}. From the identified coarse transition B=A^m and coarse innovation covariance, give a terminating sound-and-complete certificate for a queried transfer h_uv(z)=A_vu z/(1−A_vv z). Prove graph-recursive generic point identification for odd m through divided differences, the unavoidable same-law symmetry (A,D)↦(−A,D) and transfer ambiguity for even m, and a real-closed-field/CAD fallback that projects every singular compatible fiber jointly onto (A_vu,A_vv), returning either one rational transfer or two attained stable witnesses. Add Wald bands on an explicit regular class and globally honest inversion of a coarse lag-moment confidence region without branch selection. Credit classical Smith/Higham triangular-root recursion and the subsampling work of Gong et al., Tank–Fox–Shojaie, Hyttinen et al., and Gersing–Sögner–Deistler; frame Gong et al.'s Temperature–Ozone example only as a conditional m=2 Gaussian ambiguity audit under an externally defensible ordering. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The score-blind presolve derived the graph path expansion (A^m)_vu=A_vu C_m(A_vv,A_uu)+R, proved C_m positive off (0,0) for odd m and zero exactly at opposite persistences for even m, and verified the three-node rational witness including its indirect-path remainder. It derived the open singular fiber |a|<sqrt(q2/q1), the global even-factor sign obstruction, and the exact polynomial test for equality of full transfers. Zero diagonals, absent edges, open fibers, covariance filtering, zero-edge transfers, input encoding, branch mergers, and current collisions were checked. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove and calibrate an explicit uniform Gaussian quadratic-form confidence region for overlapping stationary lag moments on the compact stable class, with finite-sample constants and rational outward rounding, so semialgebraic inversion has advertised global coverage. EARLY KILL TEST: Exact CAD on d=2,m=3 with B=0 and diagonal Q must return two interior transfer-distinct witnesses, and every nonzero-edge d=2,m=2 case must retain the global sign pair; any singleton, endpoint-only witness, or lost sign pair stops the launch. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_subsampled_processdag_root_certificate.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a queried fine-grid transfer h_uv(z)=A_vu z/(1−A_vv z) in a labeled lower-triangular Gaussian VAR(1) be decided by a terminating sound-and-complete formula-or-ambiguity certificate from its subsampled law (B=A^m,Q), with a sharp odd-versus-even sampling frontier?

source_refs.claim: The paper studies recovery of causal-frequency VAR relations from subsampled observations and states that Gaussian solutions are generally nonunique.
source_refs.author: Mingming Gong, Kun Zhang, Bernhard Schölkopf, Dacheng Tao, Philipp Geiger

source_refs.claim: Identifiability of subsampled structural VARs is obtained using non-Gaussian shocks rather than Gaussian second-order information.
source_refs.author: Alex Tank, Emily B. Fox, Ali Shojaie

source_refs.claim: The paper develops rational identification of frequency-domain causal effects from process-graph spectral information but does not analyze temporal-subsampling root fibers.
source_refs.author: Nicolas-Domenic Reiter, Jonas Wahl, Andreas Gerhardus, Jakob Runge

open_problems.why_unsolved: Gong et al. isolate Gaussian nonuniqueness, Tank et al. obtain recovery by adding non-Gaussian information, and Reiter et al. identify process-graph effects once the relevant fine-scale spectral object is available. Missing is a target-specific analysis of the real stable m-th-root fiber after the coarse innovation equation and graph restrictions are imposed. Standard matrix-root algorithms choose a branch instead of certifying all compatible branches, while triangular off-diagonal recursion becomes singular when a divided-difference coefficient vanishes. Searches combining subsampled Gaussian VARs, transfer functions, parity, and real-algebraic witness extraction found no sound-and-complete transfer certificate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A terminating characterization that recursively proves singleton transfer fibers on regular strata and uses real quantifier elimination on singular strata, returning either the unique rational h_uv or two attained stable (A,D) witnesses with identical (B,Q) and unequal transfers, together with a sharp odd/even regime statement.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation starts from scientific processes sampled below their causal frequency, poses fine-scale recovery directly, and foregrounds Gaussian nonuniqueness.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: causal interactions occur faster than measurements -> subsampling changes apparent VAR relations -> Gaussian coarse laws admit multiple fine explanations -> decide whether a queried fine-scale transfer is nevertheless unique or certify its ambiguity

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt Smith's entrywise recursion for p-th roots of a triangular Schur factor, replacing numerical branch choice with symbolic divided-difference equations and explicit singular-stratum tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The compatible transition satisfies A^m=B under a supplied triangular order, exactly the algebraic structure handled entry by entry by the Schur root recursion.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the delta-method derivation of graph-indexed frequency-effect estimators and Wald laws on differentiable regular strata.
method_exemplars.why_closest: On a unique smooth root branch, h_uv is a rational process-graph effect, so its derivative and Wald limit have the same compositional structure.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct an explicit finite-sample confidence region for the overlapping lag-zero and lag-one moments of a compact stable Gaussian coarse-VAR class whose semialgebraic inverse gives globally honest, branch-free confidence sets for a fine-grid causal transfer?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves stability-sensitive deviation bounds for stable Gaussian processes, but targets regularized regression and VAR estimation rather than an invertible lag-moment region.
source_refs.author: Sumanta Basu, George Michailidis

source_refs.claim: The paper gives nonasymptotic confidence intervals for covariance functions of stationary or locally stationary zero-mean Gaussian processes.
source_refs.author: Mihai Giurcanu, Vladimir Spokoiny

source_refs.claim: The paper derives asymptotic distributions, approximate confidence intervals, and Wald tests for frequency-domain process-graph causal effects.
source_refs.author: Nicolas-Domenic Reiter, Jonas Wahl, Gabriele C. Hegerl, Jakob Runge

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing results leave three obligations disconnected: explicit quadratic-form control for overlapping stationary lag products, uniform constants over a parameter-dependent compact stable class, and deterministic outward rounding that preserves coverage after inversion through a multibranch semialgebraic compatibility relation. Basu and Michailidis do not construct a jointly calibrated coarse-lag confidence body; Giurcanu and Spokoiny do not address multivariate rational encoding and fiber inversion; Reiter et al. provide local asymptotic inference after regular identification. Searches for uniform finite-sample subsampled-VAR transfer inversion found no result joining these components.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicitly and rationally outward-rounded region C_n(α) for every entry of the coarse lag-moment vector, with computable finite-sample constants and infimum coverage at least 1−α over a declared compact stable Gaussian class, plus a proof that projecting the full compatibility set over C_n(α) yields an honest confidence set for h_uv without root-branch selection.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames covariance inference around nonasymptotic coverage for stationary Gaussian processes, providing the closest motivation arc for the moment-region bottleneck.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: causal-transfer recovery depends on stationary covariance information -> empirical lag covariances are overlapping dependent quadratic forms -> pointwise asymptotic intervals do not protect singular root branches -> build a uniform finite-sample moment region and invert it globally

method_exemplars.technique: Represent each centered empirical lag moment as an indefinite Gaussian quadratic form, split its matrix into positive and negative semidefinite parts, and apply explicit trace/operator-norm exponential bounds to both tails.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A stacked finite Gaussian trajectory turns every overlapping lag-product statistic into a fixed quadratic form, handling dependence without treating the products as independent.

method_exemplars.technique: Use spectral-density stability envelopes to control the covariance operator of a finite stationary Gaussian trajectory uniformly over a stable VAR class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Quadratic-form constants depend on trace and operator norms of the stacked trajectory covariance, for which spectral stability supplies natural uniform bounds.

method_exemplars.technique: Use rational derivatives of graph-indexed causal effects to recover conventional Wald bands on regular singleton strata while retaining confidence-region inversion elsewhere.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the local-inference benchmark the globally honest procedure should match wherever the inverse map is differentiable.

open_problems.open_problem: Does process-DAG sparsity induce a variable ordering for the polynomial system A^m=B plus the coarse innovation equations that yields a graph-height or treewidth complexity bound for exact transfer certification while preserving complete witness extraction?

source_refs.claim: The paper shows how variable orderings based on chordal structure can preserve correlative sparsity during CAD projection and reduce projection-polynomial growth.
source_refs.author: Haokun Li, Bican Xia, Huiying Zhang, Tao Zheng

source_refs.claim: The paper develops variety and layered sub-CADs that retain only cells required for a specified semialgebraic task.
source_refs.author: David J. Wilson, Russell J. Bradford, James H. Davenport, Matthew England

source_refs.claim: The paper demonstrates that exploiting logical structure can substantially improve exact search for causal structures compatible with subsampling.
source_refs.author: Antti Hyttinen, Sergey Plis, Matti Järvisalo, Frederick Eberhardt, David Danks

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic real quantifier elimination is doubly exponential, making a complete CAD fallback potentially unusable as dimension grows. Chordal-CAD savings require favorable correlative sparsity under a suitable elimination order, but A^m and accumulated innovation covariance create fill-in along directed paths, so the supplied DAG's topological order need not be a perfect elimination order for the compatibility polynomials. The first missing proof step is a bound on the induced fill graph in terms of ancestor closure, a moralized graph, or elimination-tree height. Searches pairing chordal CAD with subsampled VAR transfer certification found no such result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sufficient-condition theorem mapping a class of supplied process DAGs to an explicit CAD variable order and bounding projection degree or cell count by graph height or treewidth, together with a sound-and-complete procedure that still decides transfer constancy and extracts two exact stable witnesses when constancy fails.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates exact subsampling recovery as a constraint problem whose scientific usefulness depends on exploiting structure for scalability.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: subsampling recovery is combinatorially underdetermined -> exact compatibility constraints retain every valid fine model -> generic solvers scale poorly -> exploit the supplied causal graph to obtain a complete graph-parameterized transfer certificate

method_exemplars.technique: Construct the correlative-sparsity graph of the compatibility polynomials, choose a perfect elimination ordering where available, and track preservation of sparsity through CAD projection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired complexity result must convert graph sparsity into bounded projection-polynomial growth without weakening exact quantifier elimination.

method_exemplars.technique: Restrict lifting to the compatibility variety and cells relevant to transfer equality or inequality while retaining exact algebraic sample points as witnesses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The certificate needs the compatible fiber and its transfer projection, not a decomposition of the entire ambient parameter space.

method_exemplars.technique: Eliminate regular triangular-root coordinates recursively before invoking CAD, leaving only collision strata and innovation constraints for algebraic decomposition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Triangular recursion can shrink the CAD variable set and exposes precisely where graph-recursive elimination fails.

open_problems.open_problem: Without a supplied causal ordering, when is a labeled fine-grid transfer invariant across every permutation-triangular stable Gaussian root compatible with a subsampled law, and when can order uncertainty itself be certified by transfer-distinct witnesses?

source_refs.claim: The paper recovers lagged and instantaneous causal structure without prior causal ordering by exploiting independent non-Gaussian shocks.
source_refs.author: Alex Tank, Emily B. Fox, Ali Shojaie

source_refs.claim: The paper searches for all system-timescale causal structures compatible with measurement-timescale information and emphasizes underdetermination under subsampling.
source_refs.author: Antti Hyttinen, Sergey Plis, Matti Järvisalo, Frederick Eberhardt, David Danks

source_refs.claim: The paper identifies graph separation information and rational frequency-domain effects from process-level spectral constraints.
source_refs.author: Nicolas-Domenic Reiter, Jonas Wahl, Andreas Gerhardus, Jakob Runge

open_problems.why_unsolved: Tank et al. use non-Gaussian independent-component information to orient structural models, whereas a Gaussian subsampled law supplies only second-order restrictions. Hyttinen et al. retain an equivalence class of system-timescale graphs but study qualitative graph compatibility, and process-graph effect results start from stronger fine-scale information. Missing is simultaneous elimination over causal orders and stable real matrix-root branches, including the possibility that A is not identified but the queried rational transfer is invariant. Searches for target-specific completeness in the Gaussian, unknown-order, subsampled-VAR setting found no result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite characterization and terminating decision procedure over all compatible topological orders and stable Gaussian roots that returns a single rational h_uv exactly when the transfer is order-and-root invariant, and otherwise returns two same-law, transfer-distinct witnesses together with their orderings.

writing_exemplar.why: It treats unknown causal ordering as a first-class obstacle and separates information supplied by non-Gaussian shocks from information in subsampled second moments.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: subsampling obscures fine causal structure -> an externally supplied order is often unavailable -> non-Gaussianity can recover order but Gaussianity cannot use that route -> characterize whether the causal transfer survives joint order and root ambiguity

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt complete constraint-based enumeration of compatible system-timescale graphs, enriching each discrete candidate with polynomial root, diagonal-innovation, stability, and transfer-equality constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems require completeness across an equivalence class induced by subsampling; the destination asks whether a numerical causal functional is invariant over that class.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over graph-specific rational effect derivatives within each regular order-root cell and combine cells through confidence-region inversion rather than post-selection conditioning.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each regular compatible cell yields a rational process effect, while the unresolved inference issue is validity across the union of cells.

open_problems.open_problem: For a known ordered Gaussian VARMA(p,r) process with r>p observed under a fixed mixed-frequency stock/flow scheme, can graph restrictions make a queried fine-grid process transfer point identified even when the full high-frequency VARMA parameter is not locally identified?

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that mixed-frequency VMA and VARMA models with moving-average order above autoregressive order typically fail even local parameter identification because unobserved autocovariances can vary.
source_refs.author: Manfred Deistler, Lukas Koelbl, Brian D. O. Anderson

source_refs.claim: For multivariate autoregressions, population second moments generically identify high-frequency parameters under stock, flow, and general linear mixed-frequency observations.
source_refs.author: Brian D. O. Anderson, Manfred Deistler, Elisabeth Felsenstein, Bernd Funovits, Lukas Koelbl, Mohsen Zamani

source_refs.claim: The paper demonstrates target-specific rational identification of frequency-domain causal effects in process-graph models, motivating separation of functional identification from full parameter recovery.
source_refs.author: Nicolas-Domenic Reiter, Jonas Wahl, Andreas Gerhardus, Jakob Runge

open_problems.why_unsolved: Deistler et al. prove parameter nonidentifiability through high-frequency autocovariances invisible to the mixed-frequency scheme, but parameter nonidentifiability does not imply that every causal transfer varies along those directions. Anderson et al.'s constructive recovery stops at the VAR or lower-MA-order frontier, while target-specific process-graph identification suggests that a functional can survive nuisance nonidentification. The first changed proof step is to parameterize the free autocovariance directions subject to the ordered graph and test whether the transfer polynomial is constant on each compatible component. Searches found no transfer-level refinement of this VARMA nonidentifiability frontier.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient semialgebraic criterion, for fixed (p,r) and sampling scheme, deciding whether the projected compatible fiber of a specified rational process transfer is a singleton, together with either an identifying formula or two stable ordered VARMA witnesses having the same observed mixed-frequency law and different transfers.

writing_exemplar.why: It clearly contrasts successful mixed-frequency VAR retrieval with the free-autocovariance mechanism causing VARMA nonidentifiability.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: mixed-frequency second moments can retrieve high-frequency VARs -> moving-average components leave fine autocovariances unseen -> full VARMA parameters vary along an observational fiber -> test whether a named causal transfer is constant on that fiber

method_exemplars.technique: Use the blocked-process and extended Yule–Walker construction to separate moments fixed by the sampling scheme from unresolved high-frequency covariance coordinates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives a constructive coordinate system for the observed-law map whose fibers must be projected onto the causal transfer.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode stability, stock/flow moment matching, graph zeros, and transfer equality as real polynomial formulas and use truth-directed partial CAD to decide constancy and extract witnesses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested criterion is a projection and emptiness problem for a semialgebraic compatible fiber.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt missing-data state-space likelihood and exact Kalman E-steps to estimate regular mixed-frequency compatible components before transfer projection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies an estimation construction tailored to subsampled and mixed-frequency structural autoregressions, though the Gaussian multibranch target requires set-valued inference.

literature_map:
Gong et al. (2015, ICML) establish the central tension: subsampled Gaussian VAR laws generally do not uniquely recover fine temporal causal relations, while non-Gaussian innovations can restore identifiability.
Tank, Fox, and Shojaie (2019, Biometrika) give structural-VAR identifiability and likelihood-based estimation under non-Gaussian shocks for subsampled and mixed-frequency data.
Hyttinen et al. (2017, IJAR) formulate recovery of all compatible system-timescale graphs as an exact constraint problem, preserving ambiguity rather than forcing a singleton.
Anderson et al. (2016, Econometric Theory) prove constructive generic recovery of high-frequency VAR parameters from several mixed-frequency second-moment schemes.
Deistler, Koelbl, and Anderson (2017, Econometrics and Statistics) show an opposing VARMA phenomenon: unseen autocovariances produce typical local nonidentification when the MA order exceeds the AR order.
Gersing, Sögner, and Deistler (arXiv:2204.05952) extend mixed-frequency retrieval questions to unit-root VAR systems, illustrating model-class dependence of the retrieval frontier.
Eichler's time-series path-diagram and graphical work supplies causal graph foundations but does not settle recovery of fine-grid transfers from a subsampled law.
Reiter et al. (arXiv:2305.11561) develop process-graph path and trek rules, while Reiter et al. (Bernoulli 2026; arXiv:2406.17422) study rational identification of frequency-domain effects.
Reiter et al. (2024; arXiv:2406.18191) provide asymptotic Wald inference for process-graph effects, leaving global multibranch and finite-sample inversion untreated.
Smith (2003, SIMAX) gives the closest triangular p-th-root recursion; Bini, Higham, and Meini analyze matrix-root branches and stable algorithms, but these methods select roots rather than certify causal-law fibers.
Collins and Collins–Hong provide complete real quantifier elimination and partial CAD; Wilson et al. (2014) and Li et al. (2023) show how variety restriction and chordal sparsity can reduce CAD cost.
Basu and Michailidis (2015, Annals of Statistics) supply spectral stability measures and dependent-Gaussian deviation bounds for stable time series.
Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang (2012, ECP) provide explicit Gaussian/sub-Gaussian quadratic-form tails, and Giurcanu–Spokoiny (2004) give nonasymptotic covariance-function confidence intervals.
The inference literature does not combine overlapping multivariate lag moments, uniform stable-class constants, rational outward rounding, and branch-free semialgebraic inversion for a causal transfer.
Targeted searches found no occupied paper combining ordered Gaussian subsampled-VAR root fibers, graph-recursive divided differences, parity-specific transfer ambiguity, exact CAD witness extraction, and globally honest moment-region inversion.
